description: Rank-average ensemble of RF on RDKit descriptors+Morgan FP, a precomputed-kernel Tanimoto SVM, and LightGBM on descriptors.
Replace the RF input with descriptors+MACCS+Morgan counts (1024) and add a 500-tree ExtraTrees (min_samples_leaf=2) next to RF 500 trees in the rank-averaged ensemble.
Cut forest cost by lowering max_features to 0.08 and trees to 200 in the RF and ExtraTrees, using full-line SEARCH matches.
Replace the LightGBM member with sklearn HistGradientBoostingClassifier on descriptors in the rank-average ensemble.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The new module-level _DESC_CACHE is keyed only on the SMILES string. It stores RDKit descriptor values, which are deterministic and contain no labels, so sharing it across folds leaks nothing. It only saves compute.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. HistGradientBoostingClassifier's default early_stopping='auto' only turns on above 10000 samples, so it stays off here and no internal validation split is taken. The removed 'names' variable was not used.

The candidate is 0.0018 worse than the incumbent (0.0927 vs 0.0909). That is well within noise with one run each, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers. Swapping LightGBM for sklearn's HistGB adds nothing in simplicity or score. The descriptor cache is a harmless speed-up that could be kept on its own.
Recomputed z = (0.0909 - 0.0927) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) ≈ -0.26, which matches the reported -0.262 up to rounding.

description: Cache per-molecule RDKit descriptors, the slow part recomputed for every one of the 15 fits, so each unique SMILES is computed only once.
Set the RF to 800 trees, min_samples_leaf=2 and max_features='sqrt' to reduce variance.
Append counts of carboxylic acid, sulfonamide, quaternary N, basic aliphatic amine and phosphate SMARTS patterns to the RDKit descriptor matrix used by the RF and LightGBM.
Feed the LightGBM member RDKit descriptors plus 1024-bit Morgan count fingerprints, with 400 trees and colsample 0.3.
Cache per-molecule RDKit descriptors across folds (the dominant cost, recomputed 15 times) and cut RF max_features to 0.1 to speed up the forest.
Replace the binary Tanimoto kernel in the SVC with a MinMax kernel on radius-3 Morgan count fingerprints, computed in row chunks.
Replace the memory-heavy O(n*m*2048) broadcast minmax kernel with a fast matmul-based thresholded min-sum (counts clipped at 4).
Train the LightGBM member only on low-dimensional surface descriptors (SlogP_VSA, SMR_VSA, PEOE_VSA, EState_VSA, TPSA, MolLogP), leaving the RF and SVM unchanged.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement. The diff adds no file or network access, no pasted labels and no use of test labels. clean_mol (keep the largest fragment, then uncharge) is a per-molecule step that needs no labels and runs the same way on train and test SMILES.
No bug that makes the result meaningless. If a SMILES fails to parse, the except branch returns None again, but the incumbent would fail on the same input, so this is not a new problem.
Minor: clean_mol runs twice per molecule, once for fingerprints and once for descriptors. This costs some extra time but does not affect correctness.

z recomputed: (0.0909 - 0.0896) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) = 0.0013 / 0.00693 = 0.188, which matches the harness. The gain is far below the noise level, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers.

description: Keep only the largest fragment of each molecule and neutralize charges before computing fingerprints and descriptors.

Feed the RF only a hand-chosen physchem subset (MolWt, logP, TPSA, HBD/HBA, rotatable bonds, Fsp3, rings, aromatic rings, formal charge, acid and basic amine counts) plus Morgan bits, leaving SVM and LightGBM unchanged.
Weight each training sample by 1/sqrt(Murcko scaffold count) in the random forest fit.
Add atom-pair and torsion count features to the SVM kernel
Stacked RF and GBM via logistic blend
Label smoothing for RF via regression
